links.outcome: Readability (Flesch-Kincaid grade level) of LLM responses to patient heart failure and cardiomyopathy questions
links.effect: Most readable model (Gemini) still scored Flesch-Kincaid Grade 11.3 ± 1.9 with 668.7 ± 116.1 words; linguistic complexity and length varied substantially across models.
links.quote: Gemini provided the most readable responses (Flesch-Kincaid Grade 11.3 ± 1.9) but was among the most verbose (668.7 ± 116.1 words).

links.outcome: Hallucination and confabulation frequency in LLM patient-information responses
links.effect: Confabulation avoidance scored consistently high across models (4.49 ± 0.02 on 1-5 scale); major errors or hallucinations rare but not absent.
links.quote: While major factual errors or hallucinations were rare in our blinded evaluation, they were not entirely absent.

screen.reason: The study benchmarks the performance of multiple commercial LLMs on patient-oriented heart failure and cardiomyopathy queries using expert clinician and student raters, but does not evaluate a specific organizational deployment practice or safeguard.
